p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of fatty acid entry into mitochondria via the acyl-carnitine/carnitine transporter. To the left is mitochondria that has a box at the edge with a large white arrow (as an inset) pointing to cytosol. This image has three columns to the right cytosol, intermembrane space, and matrix. The first is cytosol. At the top and to the right of the mitochondria is C, which double bonds up and right to O, bonds left to R, and down and right to S-CoA. A curved arrow points from this down to CoA-SH. To the right of the arrow is another curved arrow that tangents to the first pointing from carnitine in a yellow box to carnitine in a yellow box. Both carnitines are on the outer mitochondrial membrane. The inside of the curved arrow has C, which double bonds up and right to O, bonds left to R, and bonds right and down to the second carnitine mentioned above. This arrow goes through a blue circle, labeled as carnitine acyltransferase-1. The second column is the intermembrane space. On the right is the inner mitochondrial space. A purple transporter sits on this membrane and crosses over to the last column, labeled as matrix. An arrow points from the second carnitine through the transporter and points to C, which double bonds up and right to O, bonds left to R, and down and right to carnitine. From here, a curved arrow points to carnitine, represented by a large blue 3-dimensional structure. From this carnitine is an arrow going through the transporter and going back left to the first carnitine. The top of the large 3-D structure is labeled as carnitine acyltransferase 2. To the right of curved arrow in the matrix is another curved arrow pointing from CoA-SH up, left, and around to C, which double bonds up and right to O, left to R, and down and right to S-CoA.
